axioms: A single executor_model field per outcome record cannot attribute credit correctly when escalation produced the passing artifact at a different tier than the one originally routed.

An acceptance criterion is only a valid validator rubric if it resolves to a machine-checkable check (shell exit code, file existence, structural diff); semantic-judgment criteria ('follows the intended design') silently degrade the gate back to judgment-based review.
2-3 pilot items is a pipeline smoke test, not a statistically sufficient sample size for a binary pass/fail metric that gates autonomy widening.

Raw pass-rate aggregated by (author_tier, executor_tier) without controlling for task difficulty conflates tier capability with selection-biased task complexity (fable/frontier is reserved for already-failed hard tasks by doctrine).
A single validator dispatch is one noisy sample; without inter-run/inter-validator agreement checks, the north-star metric may measure judge-noise rather than plan-conformance.
The metric that gates autonomy must be measuring the tier-capability signal, not confounds (attribution error, difficulty, judge variance).
primitives: plan_execution_outcome record (author/executor/validator model, criteria pass/fail, escalation_count)
failure_mode: Assumes escalation events are triggered and recorded correctly upstream (owned by escalation-retry-ladder); reviews only the aggregation/attribution downstream.
Downstream of routing correctness — assumes routing_decisions captured the right model; concerned only with the pass-rate math and rubric objectivity.
Reasons in statistical-confound terms; does not surface mechanism-level code bugs (Model copy, counter conflation) or metaphor-driven structural risks (spillway, forge).
